projects.title: Salvo: E-commerce After-Sales Intelligent Customer Service Agent Platform
projects.summary:
GitHub: github.com/li02045617/Salvo
Project Summary: For e-commerce after-sales scenarios, designed and implemented an intelligent customer service platform based on a LangGraph-controlled single-Agent architecture, connecting the complete loop of intent recognition, layered memory, RAG tool retrieval, human-handoff tickets, monitoring feedback and automatic evaluation, solving problems such as inaccurate recognition of complex intents, weak knowledge recall, easily lost multi-turn context, unobservable runtime state, and difficulty evaluating and optimizing after launch.
Agent Runtime & Business Flow: Based on LangGraph, designed a controlled single-Agent workflow that organizes intent recognition, tool calling, result verification and failure downgrade / human handoff into a controllable execution chain; the tool layer encapsulates capabilities uniformly through the MCP specification, providing caching, circuit breaking, timeout and downgrade capabilities; through tool whitelists and conditional constraints on Agent behavior, supports multi-task execution and exception fallback; the front end implements an Agent-trace trajectory panel to track Agent decisions and tool execution in real time.
Multi-Route Fusion Intent Recognition: Combined LLM semantic classification, Embedding similarity and keyword rules for intent voting, covering 10 types of after-sales intents such as orders, refunds, logistics and returns/exchanges and 4 confidence tiers, and used an LRU cache to reduce high-frequency repeated inference calls; intent results determine the task type, and the task type dynamically controls the tool whitelist, narrowing the Agent's action space and avoiding irrelevant or unauthorized tool calls.
RAG Hybrid Retrieval Pipeline: Designed and implemented Hybrid Retrieval, fusing BM25 keyword recall and ChromaDB vector recall through RRF, achieving Query Rewrite, parallel recall, deduplication, LLM reranking and metadata filtering, together with a TTL cache and circuit-breaking/downgrade mechanism; built a business knowledge base covering 9 after-sales knowledge domains (37 documents), registered as an MCP tool for the Agent to retrieve on demand.
Retrieval Evaluation & Optimization: Built a retrieval evaluation set of 35 manually annotated Queries, comparing three strategies (direct / hybrid / rewrite) on Recall, Precision, MRR and NDCG, and raising Recall@5 from 0.31 to 0.74 through experimental iteration; supplemented end-to-end trial validation of the Agent's knowledge-retrieval tool calls and recall results, and combined it with LLM-as-Judge for end-to-end evaluation of dialogue quality on 20 customer-service cases.
Layered Memory Management: Based on Redis and vector storage, designed a three-layer memory mechanism of short-term working memory, long-term episodic memory and user profile; through context compression and dynamic splicing, controls Token spend, and supports cross-turn retrieval of historical information and reuse of the user profile.

projects.title: Mini-dsh: A Coding Agent Harness Based on a Plugin Architecture
projects.summary:
GitHub: github.com/li02045617/mini-dsh
Project Summary: Drawing on the 'everything is a plugin' design philosophy of DeepSeek Harness, implemented a lightweight Coding Agent Harness from scratch in TypeScript/Node.js, modularizing the Agent's core capabilities into replaceable plugins, and quantifying the impact of different Harness mechanisms on Agent execution results through Benchmarks and ablation experiments.
Plugin-based Agent Runtime: Implemented MiniContext, PluginRegistry and ServiceRegistry around the MiniPlugin/Service protocol, using Plugin/Service abstractions to decouple Model, Tool, Session, Permission, Event, Context Manager and Agent Loop; through dependency validation, Service injection and lifecycle management, plugins run and can be independently replaced without modifying the execution loop.
Agent Loop & Tool Execution: Implemented multi-state progression of Model, Tool and Result, configured with 64 model-request rounds, 128 tool calls, a 10-minute task timeout and AbortController cancellation; based on the native Tool-Calling capability, abstracted a unified ModelRequest/ModelResponse, mapped the structured interface of model returns to a unified tool execution interface, and provided file operations and run_command basic tools.
Session & Context Management: Persists complete messages, tool calls and results with append-only JSONL, supporting Session recovery and /continue after model budget is exhausted; the Context Manager triggers model summarization at an 80% threshold, retaining only the latest 12 messages and truncating large tool results to mitigate context bloat in long-range tasks; additionally designed a Prompt Optimizer plugin that converts vague requirements into executable Worker Prompts, reducing the impact of unclear task constraints on execution.
Benchmark Design & Ablation Experiments: Built a self-designed 20-task Benchmark + automatic Evaluator covering code comprehension, bug fixing, feature implementation, refactoring and test writing; with unified model, permissions and budget, ran comparative experiments across Baseline / Context Manager / Prompt Optimizer / Full Harness, computing 6 categories of metrics including success rate, Model Rounds, Tool Calls/Errors, Token and Latency: Full Harness reached a 90% (18/20) success rate vs. 75% (15/20) for the Baseline, while the average number of model responses, the number of tool failures and Token consumption all decreased, validating the effectiveness of the Harness.
